Triggers let you define what needs to happen for an Effect to take place. To program a Trigger, place it in a room, double click on it and set it up! You need to stack an Effect with the Trigger to make it work.

Effects are what happens after you activate a Trigger. To program an Effect, place it in your room, double click on it and set it up! You will always need to stack a Trigger with the Effect to make it work.
Conditions are specific things that need to be done before a Trigger will work. If you want to use a Condition, you will need to stack it with a Trigger and Effect.
Use Selectors to specify users and/or furni that will be used in Wired. For example, "WIRED Selector: Users in team" combined with "WIRED Effect: Teleport to furni" teleports an entire team at once!
Add-Ons are a special type of Wired that is used to add extra configurations to an existing Wired stack. Each Add-On has its own unique purpose.
Discover a new branch Wired - Wired Variables!
How do Wired Variables work?

Variables are used to store values and read them at a later point with Wired. For example, they can be used to store the amount of health points for a user. Variables can belong to users, furni, or even the entire room! You can share them across multiple rooms too. But how do you use them?

Wired Variables work different from all existing Wired boxes, because they are not stacked on top of the usual Wired boxes, like Triggers and Effect. Instead, Wired Variables form a new kind of Wired stack (lets call it a "Variable stack"), one that defines how the Variable works.

In a usual Wired stack, a Wired Effect is stacked on a Wired Trigger. In a Variable stack, there is one "WIRED Variable" and additionally you can add Variable Add-Ons on top of the stack to bring further configurations to the Wired Variable. The boxes that go on a Variable stack all share a similar design, so it's easy to know if a box belongs on a Variable!

The Wired boxes on this page is a combination of the types of Wired you all know and love, like Triggers, Effects and Conditions. The ones on this page are used specifically to work with Wired Variables
